newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Annan to get Carlsson group support for UN reforms.
newsitem.headline: Annan to get Carlsson group support for UN reforms.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan is expected to get backing for his U.N. reforms from an influential group of countries at the start of a tour of Nordic countries on Sunday.
Annan unveiled a package of proposals in July to overhaul the 52-year-old U.N. bureaucracy, shrink budgets, merge programmes and put the money saved to work in poor nations.
Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson is set to convey to Annan the full support of the "Carlsson group" involving high ranking representatives of 16 heads of state, his spokeswoman said.
The group was set up by former Swedish Prime Minister Ingvar Carlsson in 1995 to take part in reforming and strengthening the United Nations.
"We are hoping everything will be ready so we can present this document, signed by all the heads of state, on Sunday," Persson's spokeswoman Ingrid Iremark told Reuters.

The Carlsson group brings together Sweden, Canada, Australia, Mexico, Japan, Brazil, the Netherlands, India, South Africa, Egypt, Jamaica, the Ivory Coast, the Republic of Korea, Indonesia, the Czech Republic, and Ireland.
Its document welcomes Annan's fast start on reform and calls for the proposals to be implemented as soon as possible to gear the U.N. more effectively to priorities set by its members.
Annan's meetings with Persson and Swedish Foreign Minister Lena Hjelm-Wallen kick off a four-week trip to Sweden, Finland, Denmark, Norway and Iceland that is part official and part holiday.

Annan moves on to Finland on Tuesday to meet all the country's top officials, but international attention is expected to focus on a meeting with Elisabeth Rehn, the Finnish U.N. Special Rapporteur on Human Rights.

Last year the U.N. Committee on Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) criticised Finnish authorities for playing down racism, expressing "deep concern over the significant increase of racially motivated acts and violence in Finland".

Annan will return to Sweden for a holiday with his Swedish wife of 13 years, lawyer Nina Lagergren, who is a member of the powerful Wallenberg family. They have a holiday house at Blekinge in southern Sweden.
He then goes to Denmark on an official visit on September 1-2, and to Norway on September 2-4.

Apat from meeting Norwegian Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland and Foreign Minister Bjorn Tore Godal, he will have lunch with King Harald and Queen Sonja and participate in a conference to formulate a treaty on an international ban of anti-personnel mines.
His last stop will be Iceland on September 4-5.
